findings.reason: a node following §3 deletes schema slots whose own field description keeps them "only so an existing host file that sets it keeps loading", so with `extra="forbid"` the host config stops loading and three test files the plan does not touch go red.
findings.text: §3 deletes the four flight keys (`on_fail`, `reflex`, `spelling`, `max_concurrent_runs`) as "declared and read by no code" and confirms only against "every `docs/state/*/flight.yaml` named by mounts.json", but `max_concurrent_runs` is set in the host layer (`~/.config/reckon/flight.yaml:462` sets it to 64) and is asserted readable by `tests/test_backend_carries_no_worker_cap.py:249` ("the key stays readable") and `tests/test_lane_concurrency_ceiling.py:260`, while `on_fail` is set in the shipped defaults (`reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml:106`, `on_fail: hold`) and asserted resolvable by `tests/test_flight.py:879` (`resolved.origin("gates.on_fail") == "shipped"`); the mounted-projects check reads none of those layers

findings.reason: the gate can report pass while the suite is red, so the measure cannot observe the breakage the section causes and does not gate the node.
findings.text: §3's done-when builds its test list only from "the tests importing the touched modules", which excludes `tests/test_backend_carries_no_worker_cap.py`, `tests/test_lane_concurrency_ceiling.py` and `tests/test_flight.py` — the tests that assert the deleted flight keys survive

findings.reason: a worker completing §2 cannot close it on its stated measure and must either guess §4's outcome or re-open §2 after §4, an ordering the plan should settle rather than the worker.
findings.text: §2's done-when requires the ratchet allowlist to be "exactly the modules still unreached after §3 and §4", but §4 is declared to run "after §2", so §2 cannot satisfy its own measure until §4 has run
